title: Reading a study through its evidence
summary: A working guide to connect the question, design, sample, measurement and findings in one record.
rawText: Reading a study through its evidence A working guide to connect the question, design, sample, measurement and findings in one record. Start with what the study tests Record the question, design, sample, country, setting and follow-up separately. Spirituality, religiosity, religious coping, integration preference and practice should not be entered as interchangeable constructs. Identify the instrument, respondent and measurement time for each variable. Record findings with their limits Record the comparator, main outcome, reported effect size and confidence interval. When only an abstract is available, do not infer missing methods. Do not label a cross-sectional association a causal effect. Examine selection bias, missing data, cultural context, funding and conflicts of interest separately. Separate a study from a synthesis A review additionally needs its scope, search date, information sources, eligibility criteria and selection decisions documented. PRISMA guides reporting, not a standalone quality score. The template here supports extraction. It is not a completed review or a risk-of-bias instrument.

title: Spiritual experience and counseling
summary: A starting point for understanding the person’s experience, meaning and preferences before applying a label.
rawText: Spiritual experience and counseling A starting point for understanding the person’s experience, meaning and preferences before applying a label. Start with the person’s language Faith, belonging, conscience or the meaning of life may arise in a conversation. None automatically establishes a spiritual need. Our proposed starting point is to ask what the person means in their own words. Requiring the label “spirituality” and imposing that label are two different ways of narrowing the conversation. Discussion is not consent to a practice Sharing a topic is not the same as requesting a religious practice or the practitioner’s interpretation. Someone may want to describe prayer without wanting to pray together during a session. This educational note proposes discussing the topic’s importance, the wish to address it, and consent to a particular method separately. Resources, struggles and goals As you read, consider three separate notes: what this experience means, what supports or troubles the person, and what help they want. Nonbelief should not be treated as a deficit. Not discussing spirituality is also a valid preference. These are proposed areas of inquiry, not a scale or fixed intervention sequence.

title: Evaluating research findings
summary: A short reading structure that separates research, interpretation and recommendation.
rawText: Evaluating research findings A short reading structure that separates research, interpretation and recommendation. The studies may ask different questions One study may examine client preferences, another religious similarity and another adapted treatment outcomes. Rather than treating them as repetitions of one finding, write down each actual question. This site displays source type separately from the title. The existence of guidance does not mean an intervention effect has been measured. Keep the comparator visible In Captari and colleagues’ meta-analysis, the more rigorous additive comparisons found no significant advantage for psychological distress, but better spiritual well-being. Keep these outcomes separate. A nonsignificant difference does not prove equivalence. The record also does not automatically establish the effect of a specific theory-based spiritual integration. Write your inference separately Test a reading note with three sentences: what the source directly shows, what it does not show, and what new question it raises. The last sentence may be your interpretation or recommendation; do not report it as a finding. Reporting checklists support transparency but cannot themselves repair a design problem.

title: Competence and ethics in counseling
summary: Keeping the relationship between the client’s wishes and the practitioner’s capabilities explicit.
rawText: Competence and ethics in counseling Keeping the relationship between the client’s wishes and the practitioner’s capabilities explicit. Similarity is not competence Start from the assumption that a shared worldview does not guarantee understanding. The proposed self-check is whether we hear the actual request or mistake personal comfort for competence. Disagreement alone does not establish that working together is impossible. Specific knowledge, skills and limits require separate consideration. Being able to disagree Collaboration should not mean agreeing with every interpretation. A proposed conversational stance is: “Am I understanding you correctly; what needs changing?” That sentence alone does not remove unequal power. How refusal is received and whose request shapes the goal matter too. Making limits visible Explain the rationale, intended function and alternatives of a proposed practice. Consider appropriate supervision and support at competence limits. Educational content here does not make individualized decisions. A crisis or immediate risk should not be managed through a web reading; use local emergency and professional support channels.

title: Cultural context and worldview
summary: Considering belonging, support, commitment and constrained options without reducing one to another.
rawText: Cultural context and worldview Considering belonging, support, commitment and constrained options without reducing one to another. From label to experience Religious or cultural affiliation alone does not tell us what someone wants in counseling. This dossier proposes following a question about affiliation with inquiry into its lived meaning. The same community may be experienced as supportive and difficult. Keeping both possibilities open challenges a single, uniform notion of culture. Noticing metaphysical assumptions Hodge offers a theoretical discussion of metaphysical assumptions in mental health discourse. One reading question is whether practitioners treat their own position as the sole standard of neutrality. This is not a claim that all metaphysical views are clinically identical or that one is more effective. Commitment and available options A commitment can be meaningful while surrounded by difficult conditions. We propose distinguishing what the person wants to preserve, available options and the cost of acting differently. Staying or leaving is not predetermined as success. Respect for culture should not make concrete harm or safety needs invisible.

title: Selecting assessment instruments
summary: Four separate checks for construct, intended use, translation and rights.
rawText: Selecting assessment instruments Four separate checks for construct, intended use, translation and rights. Look beyond the name Spiritual well-being, spiritual struggle, religious commitment and preference for integration are not the same measurement. Start by naming the construct in your question. Then inspect what the instrument measures, in which population and for what purpose. Popularity is not evidence that a tool fits your question. Translation, adaptation and permission When reviewing an instrument, record language, permission and research on the target population separately. The catalogue proposes checking the adaptation study and use conditions alongside the original publication. Finding a form online should not be turned into an assumption that it can be republished or is valid for another population. Create an instrument record Keep original source, version, target population, response format, permissions and adaptation study in separate fields. When information is missing, record the gap rather than guessing. This catalog is a starting point for selection. It does not produce diagnoses, automated scores or clinical decisions.

summary: Compare views of the person, change and boundaries rather than assembling a common technique list.
rawText: Spirituality in psychotherapy theories Compare views of the person, change and boundaries rather than assembling a common technique list. Identify the theory’s question When reading an approach, note how it explains difficulty and where it locates change. Then ask how spiritual experience enters that account. Spiritual vocabulary alone does not establish theoretical integration. Avoid treating distinct approaches as different names for the same techniques. Compare the same dimensions The proposed theory records use five fields: view of the person, explanation of difficulty, change goals, relation to spiritual experience and scope of evidence. Record tensions as well An integration note should not end with similarities. Which assumptions about autonomy, commitment, reality or change differ? This is a proposed reading question. Theoretical compatibility alone does not establish suitability for a particular person or clinical superiority. Practice decisions require separate competence and assessment.

title: AI and professional responsibility

A real title or DOI does not validate every interpretation. A professional interface does not increase the evidential strength of its content. Preserve meaning in translation “Associated with” must not become “causes” in translation. Population, context, uncertainty and source limitations should survive across languages. Any future tool needs a separately designed purpose, responsibility, access, retention and deletion framework. Technical correctness is not clinical benefit or ethics approval.
